heading: 1.1 Business Solution Summary
text:
Rogers bank currently uses outsourced vendors for Contact Centre Technology. The Contact Centre Replatform Project will replace the existing vendor owned
technology with Amazon Web Services Connect. The AWS Connect platform will serve as a Service contact centre solution that will reduce operational cost, increase
contact centre flexibility and deliver framework for an improved customer experience.

The project will deliver technology capable of enhancing the customer experience by driving improved options for self-service, and empowering contextual interactions
across Rogers Bank channels. AWS Connect solution will drive a richer interaction with Contact Centre agents, improving the customer experience by serving context
and facilitating a more personalized conversation.

heading: 1.2 Project Objectives
text:
1) Build Contact Centre platform flexibility and agility by replacing the existing technology stack with AWS Connect Contact Centre as a Service (CCaaS)
2) Implement a modernized / future ready digital platform that enables OMNI channel interactions across Rogers Bank service properties

3) Enrich Contact Centre interactions by presenting data driven context along with Al enhanced recommendations that drive customer experience.

4) Accelerate Contact Centre efficiencies through expanded self service, agent tooling automated workflows and enhanced data

heading: Overview of PCI Solution for CCR (MVP)
text:
The CCR/RBCONNECT handles sensitive customer "Account Data" as part of its core functionality. To reduce and narrow the PCI DSS compliance scope,
RBCONNECT will leverage Rogers Bank's Cardholder Data Environment (CDE), which was created as part of the PCI solution for Instant Credit (IC). This CDE design
and implementation are covered in the HLD - Card Viewer (PCI) document (referenced in the section "Referenced Documents" below).

The solution described in this HLD is designed to safeguard sensitive customer data at every stage — from initial data collection in Amazon Connect to secure
communication with TSYS and back — ensuring full compliance with PCI DSS standards.

No sensitive authentication data (PIN) is recorded, stored, or logged anywhere in the system (outside of TSYS). All processing of sensitive authentication
data is performed in volatile memory (RAM) and is not persistent. Cardholder data (PAN) is not logged anywhere in the system.

Through the use of robust encryption methods, secure credential management, and meticulous segmentation and segregation of roles and data, the system ensures
that customers can securely set, update, or verify their PINs and retrieve card information. Strong IAM policies and secure authentication and authorization
mechanisms further enhance protection, safeguarding sensitive information while enabling seamless execution of business logic.

This approach delivers a secure, efficient, and user-friendly customer experience.

heading: Verify PIN Use Case - ASYNC API Requests:
text:
For verifying a PIN, the Lambda function checks all four PIN positions against TSYS asynchronously to optimize performance.

The Lambda function sends four independent ASYNC API requests to TSYS, each checking a specific PIN position.

These requests are processed in parallel, meaning the "request" does not wait for the server's response before continuing,

Once all responses are received, the Lambda function aggregates them and compares them to form a consolidated result (Success/Fail).
The aggregated result is returned to the caller, ensuring efficient and accurate PIN verification.

The workflow is blocking, meaning no further processing occurs until the response is received.

Processing all PIN positions in parallel significantly speeds up the verification process.

heading: Architecture Overview:
text:
Amazon Connect integrates with TSYS back-end systems via AWS Lambdas in the Cardholder Data Environment (CDE). All egress to TSYS passes through AWS

Network Firewall (with domain-based filtering) and the NAT Gateway, maintaining a secure, PCl-compliant path:

heading: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for Access:
text: Amazon Connect enforces MFA for all user and administrator access, ensuring secure authentication to meet compliance requirements.

heading: No PIN in Call and Screen Recordings:
text:
Sensitive Authentication Data (SAD) are not captured in call and screen recordings within Amazon Connect, adhering to PCI DSS guidelines and ensuring

sensitive data is not inadvertently exposed.

heading: PCI Data in Transit:
text:
All PCI data transmitted from the Cardholder Data Environment (CDE) to TSYS (Rogers Bank's third-party system of record) is sent over HTTPS using TLS 1.2

or higher. Similarly, any PCI data returned by TSYS to the CDE is also transmitted via HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or higher. Beyond these secure exchanges with

TSYS, no PCI data leaves the CDE account.

functions designated for PCI-related use cases include:

© GetAccountByaNt: Retrieves customer account information using ANI match.
© Verify?in: Verifies the PIN using TSYS APIs.
© ChangePin: Updates or sets a new PIN securely.

adherence to PCI DSS standards.

heading: Enhanced Traffic Security:
text:
Security groups are configured for each Lambda function running in a VPC and are attached to the Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) created during function
execution. Inbound rules allow traffic from Amazon Connect, while outbound rules allow HTTPS (port 443) to the NAT Gateway. These security groups act as

After the Lambda sends outbound traffic, it flows to the NAT Gateway, which forwards the encrypted request to the AWS Network Firewall. The firewall then
enforces domain-based filtering (allow-listing) for TSYS before the traffic proceeds to the Internet Gateway. This design ensures that only traffic to the TSYS.
domain is permitted, providing an additional layer of security and monitoring.

heading: IAM Roles Configuration:
text:

Lambda execution environments, respectively, allowing them to securely retrieve secrets from AWS Secrets Manager without embedding credentials in the
container images or using environment variables. This approach adheres to the principle of least privilege, ensuring that each Lambda function can access only
the secrets and resources it is explicitly authorized to use. (For further info, refer to Sec 2.7.4.2)

heading: Secure Secrets Management:
text:

an expiration time, necessitating a rotation process. TSYS is expected to send notification emails in advance of expiration. This approach minimizes the risk of
credential compromise and supports compliance with security best practices and PCI DSS requirements.

text:

sensitive credentials in the Lambda code or configurations. The functions communicate with TSYS using HTTPS secured with TLS 1.2 (or higher) to ensure
end-to-end encryption of data in transit.

heading: Data Containment:
text:

segmentation and data protection standards.

Lambda functions are configured to run within CDE VPC. They are associated with an existing private subnet, ensuring secure routing and compliance with PCI

heading: Native Auto Scaling:
text:
AWS Lambda functions leverage native auto-scaling capabilities managed by AWS. The number of concurrent Lambda executions automatically scales (within
the defined account concurrency limits) based on the demand generated by Amazon Connect, ensuring high availability and responsiveness even during peak
usage periods.

The Network Firewall then applies domain-based allow-listing before directing the traffic to the Internet Gateway for TSYS Open AP! calls. This setup ensures
that only outbound connections to the TSYS domain are permitted, prevents unauthorized inbound traffic, and provides a secure, monitored path for sensitive
data.
